topics.topic: Anatomy & Physiology of the Ear (~30 questions)
subtopics: Anatomy of the external ear (pinna, external auditory canal)
Anatomy of the middle ear (tympanic membrane, ossicles, tympanic cavity boundaries, eustachian tube)
Anatomy of the inner ear (cochlea, vestibular apparatus, semicircular canals, endolymph & perilymph)
Blood supply and nerve supply of the ear
Physiology of hearing (sound conduction, impedance matching, travelling wave theory, tonotopic organization)
Physiology of balance (vestibular reflexes, VOR, otolith organs)
Tuning fork tests (Rinne, Weber, ABC — Absolute Bone Conduction)
Audiometry basics (pure tone audiometry, speech audiometry, impedance audiometry, tympanometry)
OAE (Otoacoustic Emissions) and BERA (Brainstem Evoked Response Audiometry)

topics.topic: Diseases of the External Ear (~25 questions)
subtopics: Congenital anomalies (microtia, atresia, preauricular sinus, accessory auricle)
Keratosis obturans vs cholesteatoma of external auditory canal
Exostosis and osteoma of the EAC
Tumors of the external ear (SCC, BCC)

topics.topic: Diseases of the Middle Ear — Otitis Media (~45 questions)
subtopics: Acute suppurative otitis media (ASOM) — etiology, pathology, stages, complications, management
Secretory/serous otitis media (SOM/glue ear) — etiology, pathology, management, grommet insertion
Chronic suppurative otitis media — tubotympanic (safe/mucosal) type
Cholesteatoma — congenital vs acquired, pathogenesis (retraction pocket theory, migration theory, metaplasia), complications

Complications of otitis media — intratemporal (mastoiditis, petrositis, labyrinthitis, facial nerve palsy) and intracranial (meningitis, brain abscess, lateral sinus thrombosis, otitic hydrocephalus, extradural abscess, subdural abscess)
Tympanic membrane perforations — types, healing, myringoplasty
Clinical features (Schwartze sign, Carhart's notch, paracusis Willisii)
Causes of sensorineural hearing loss (presbycusis, noise-induced, ototoxicity, sudden SNHL, Meniere's, acoustic neuroma, congenital)
Noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) — TTS, PTS, acoustic trauma
Ototoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, cisplatin, aspirin)
Cochlear implants — indications, candidacy, mechanism, rehabilitation
Clinical features (triad/tetrad — vertigo, tinnitus, hearing loss, aural fullness)
Surgical management (endolymphatic sac decompression, labyrinthectomy, vestibular neurectomy)
Lermoyez syndrome and Tumarkin's otolithic crisis
BPPV — pathophysiology (canalithiasis, cupulolithiasis), Dix-Hallpike test, Epley maneuver, Semont maneuver
Vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) — clinical features, investigations (MRI with gadolinium), management
Anatomy of the facial nerve (intracranial, intratemporal, extratemporal segments)
Bell's palsy — etiology, clinical features, grading (House-Brackmann), management
Facial nerve injury in temporal bone fractures
Facial nerve testing (Schirmer's test, stapedial reflex, taste testing, nerve excitability test, electroneuronography)

topics.topic: Anatomy & Physiology of the Nose and Paranasal Sinuses (~20 questions)
subtopics: External nose anatomy (cartilages, bones, blood supply, nerve supply)
Nasal cavity anatomy (lateral wall — turbinates, meatuses, ostia; septum; roof; floor)
Paranasal sinuses — anatomy, development, drainage pathways
Nasal cycle and physiology of nasal airflow
Functions of the nose (filtration, humidification, warming, olfaction, resonance)
Etiology — local causes (trauma, DNS, tumors, granulomas) and systemic causes (hypertension, coagulopathies, liver disease)
Deviated nasal septum — types, etiology, clinical features
Septal abscess and septal hematoma — emergency management
Allergic rhinitis — classification (ARIA), pathophysiology, skin prick test, specific IgE, management (antihistamines, intranasal steroids, immunotherapy)
Acute rhinosinusitis — etiology, pathology, clinical features, management
Chronic rhinosinusitis — with and without polyps

Complications of sinusitis — orbital (preseptal cellulitis, orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, orbital abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis) and intracranial (meningitis, brain abscess, frontal bone osteomyelitis/Pott's puffy tumor)
Fungal sinusitis — allergic fungal sinusitis (AFS), mycetoma/fungal ball, invasive fungal sinusitis (acute and chronic), mucormycosis
Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS) — principles, technique, landmarks
Frontal sinus surgery (trephination, Draf procedures, osteoplastic flap)
Ethmoidal polyps — etiology, pathology, clinical features
Nasal polyposis and association with asthma, aspirin sensitivity
Differential diagnosis (inverted papilloma, meningocele, glioma, dermoid)

topics.topic: Tumors of the Nose & Paranasal Sinuses (~18 questions)
subtopics: Benign tumors — inverted papilloma, osteoma, hemangioma, fibrous dysplasia
Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA) — clinical features, Holman-Miller sign, staging, embolization, surgical approaches
Malignant tumors — squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, esthesioneuroblastoma (olfactory neuroblastoma), melanoma, lymphoma
Maxillary sinus carcinoma — Ohngren's line, staging
Acute tonsillitis — etiology, clinical features, management
Chronic tonsillitis — clinical features, indications for tonsillectomy
Adenoid hypertrophy — clinical features (adenoid facies, mouth breathing, OSA), management
Tonsillectomy — techniques (dissection, coblation, intracapsular), complications (hemorrhage — reactionary and secondary)
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) — pathophysiology, polysomnography, management (CPAP, UPPP)

topics.topic: Pharyngitis & Diseases of the Oropharynx (~12 questions)
Larynx — Anatomy, Physiology & Voice Disorders (~25 questions)
subtopics: Anatomy of the larynx (cartilages, muscles — intrinsic and extrinsic, nerve supply — RLN, SLN, blood supply)
Vocal cord paralysis — unilateral and bilateral, causes (RLN palsy, SLN palsy), Semon's law, positions of vocal cords
Carcinoma of the larynx — glottic, supraglottic, subglottic; staging (TNM), clinical features, management
Conservation laryngeal surgery (cordectomy, vertical partial laryngectomy, supraglottic laryngectomy, supracricoid partial laryngectomy)
Total laryngectomy — technique, voice rehabilitation (esophageal speech, TEP with voice prosthesis, electrolarynx)
Neck dissection — types (radical, modified radical, selective)
Causes of stridor in children (laryngomalacia, croup, epiglottitis, foreign body, subglottic stenosis, hemangioma)
Causes of stridor in adults (tumors, bilateral vocal cord palsy, angioedema, trauma)
Assessment and grading of airway obstruction
Indications (upper airway obstruction, prolonged ventilation, pulmonary toilet, prophylactic)
Tracheostomy tubes — types (cuffed, uncuffed, fenestrated, speaking valve)

Complications — immediate (hemorrhage, pneumothorax, tube misplacement), early (tube blockage, subcutaneous emphysema, tube displacement), late (tracheal stenosis, tracheo-innominate fistula, tracheoesophageal fistula, difficult decannulation)

topics.topic: Foreign Bodies in the Aerodigestive Tract (~15 questions)
subtopics: Foreign body in the ear — types, removal techniques
Foreign body in the nose — types (button battery — emergency), complications (rhinolith), management
Foreign body in the pharynx and esophagus (coin, denture, fish bone) — clinical features, X-ray findings, management (rigid esophagoscopy)
Foreign body in the larynx and tracheobronchial tree — clinical features (choking, stridor, check-valve/ball-valve/bypass-valve mechanisms), management (rigid bronchoscopy)
Complications of foreign body aspiration (atelectasis, pneumonia, lung abscess, bronchiectasis)
Anatomy of major salivary glands (parotid, submandibular, sublingual)
Sialolithiasis (salivary calculi) — submandibular > parotid, clinical features, management
Pleomorphic adenoma (mixed tumor) — clinical features, management (superficial parotidectomy), recurrence
Other malignant tumors (acinic cell carcinoma, carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma)
Anatomy of deep neck spaces (parapharyngeal, retropharyngeal, prevertebral, submandibular, masticator)
Imaging (CT with contrast) and management principles

topics.topic: Branchial Anomalies & Congenital Neck Masses (~12 questions)
subtopics: Embryology of branchial arches, clefts, and pouches
Branchial cyst (second arch — most common), sinus, fistula
Third and fourth branchial pouch anomalies
Thyroglossal duct cyst — clinical features, Sistrunk operation
Differential diagnosis of neck masses (rule of 80s, anatomical triangle approach)
Robotic surgery in ENT (TORS — Transoral Robotic Surgery)
Hearing implants (middle ear implants, auditory brainstem implant)
Biologics in CRS with nasal polyps (dupilumab, omalizumab)
